dedupe_keys.name: oxygen systems in health facilities of 39 low and middle income countries rapid facility level assessment

description: This case study surveys whether medical oxygen is reliably available and whether oxygen system components work in health facilities across 39 low- and middle-income countries. The authors, from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Global Fund, published it as an open-access journal article. Data collectors visited 2,884 primary, secondary and tertiary facilities in six WHO subregions between September 2022 and February 2023, selected by purposive and stratified random sampling, and asked facility leaders a standard questionnaire on uninterrupted oxygen availability over three months and on sources such as cylinders, concentrators, plants and liquid oxygen, distribution, delivery devices, monitoring and quality assurance. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: sampling was partly purposive, answers are self-reported by facility leaders, and facility-level data are not released with the article. The study found reliable oxygen in only 304 of 1,241 primary facilities (24.5 percent) and 558 of 1,064 secondary facilities (52.4 percent), with better availability at tertiary level and large gaps between subregions. Simulation uses: parameterising oxygen supply and equipment availability in health system resilience, surge capacity and power-outage models for low-resource settings. Related records: the UNICEF oxygen system planning tool (model-unicef-oxygen-system-planning-tool) sizes oxygen supply and the WHO harmonized health facility assessment (data-who-harmonized-health-facility-assessment-hhfa) collects similar indicators.
